orchestrated to where a step should stay human-owned, and defend those calls once they're tested against real code.</li> <li>Discover and prioritize sources of friction across GitLab's SDLC, driving the fix — agentic, process-based, or both — from a rough hypothesis through to a shipped, measured result.</li> <li>Work across any part of GitLab's codebase as the problem requires, since this team operates like a small, generalist group rather than one scoped to a single service.</li> <li>Apply distributed systems judgment to catch cases where generated code looks correct but breaks under concurrency, at scale, or across deployment topologies (including self-managed, dedicated, and multi-tenant environments), and coach others to do the same.</li> <li>Mentor senior and mid-level engineers on agent engineering practices and distributed systems judgment, through design reviews and pairing that raise the team's collective bar rather than just your own output.</li> <li>Collaborate with the India-based group a few times a week to align on the roadmap, and represent the team's technical progress to stakeholders in the Chief Technology Officer's organization.</li> <li>Serve as a bar raiser for the team's hiring, owning the Technical Leadership round for other Staff-level candidates as the team scales.</li> <li>Own a greenfield technical foundation from day one, with your scope and impact free to grow as the team scales.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Experience building reliable agentic or large language model (LLM)-based systems, including multi-step orchestration, tool use, guardrails, and recovery.</li> <li>Ability to work autonomously in unfamiliar codebases and drive solutions from discovery through completion.</li> <li>Strong distributed systems and computer science fundamentals, including coordination, consistency, idempotency, rate limiting, failure modes, and degradation under load.</li> <li>Proficiency in Go, Rust, or Python, with the ability to read and modify code in the others.</li> <li>A track record of delivering results from unclear or incomplete requirements — able to take a complex, loosely specified problem and decompose it into a concrete proposal of small, shippable steps.</li> <li>Experience designing evaluation frameworks for systems where "looks plausible" and "is actually correct" are different questions, and a track record of raising the quality bar for a team's output, not just your own.</li> <li>A history of unblocking and enabling teammates — through design reviews, technical writing, or mentoring — and of engaging regularly with other teams to find where collaboration actually pays off.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>Nonlinear Productivity — shortened internally to "NLP," with no relation to natural language processing — is one of GitLab's newest teams: a strategic incubation group that reports into AI Platform leadership under the direct sponsorship of the CTO. It's split into a US group (this role) and an India-based group working the same charter; the two sync on roadmap and tooling a few times a week but otherwise run day to day on their own. Solutions that prove out internally are the team's path to a monetized, customer-facing GitLab offering.</p> <p>It's a good fit for engineers who want technical ownership of something with no existing playbook, and a hand in defining a brand-new part of GitLab from its first commit.</p> <div class="c-message_actions__container c-message__actions"> </div> <div><span style="font-size: xx-small;"><span style="color: white;">Remote-Global</span></span></div><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. You'll lead large backend initiatives, guide the modernization of a large monolith into modular, reusable, appropriately independent systems, and set standards that help teams move faster without compromising quality, security, reliability, or operability.</p> <p>You'll work with Product, Frontend, Infrastructure, Security, Data, Engineering Managers, and engineers across product groups. You'll lead complex backend architecture, make product trade-offs, and influence technical direction without formal authority.</p> <p>GitLab is an open core software company that develops an artificial intelligence-powered DevSecOps platform. Our mission is to enable everyone to contribute to and co-create the software that powers our world. We work in an all-remote, asynchronous environment where you communicate decisions clearly in writing and work independently.</p> <h2>What you’ll do</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Lead the technical design and delivery of backend initiatives that span teams, and identify and remove systemic bottlenecks across product and infrastructure groups.</li> <li value="2">Drive modular backend, service, data, and platform architecture, including modernization of the monolith and legacy backends while preventing fragmentation and service sprawl.</li> <li value="3">Define and improve standards for application programming interfaces, contracts, compatibility, schema evolution, testing, security, performance, observability, operability, and maintainability.</li> <li value="4">Establish patterns for dependency management, data ownership, eventing, failure isolation, service maturity, and operational documentation.</li> <li value="5">Establish Go service patterns and Kubernetes operating practices where they matter to the production estate, and guide Rust adoption where it addresses systems, security, performance, or supply-chain needs.</li> <li value="6">Take part in on-call and incident response for systems your teams own, serve as a technical escalation point during complex incidents, and turn lessons from incidents into lasting improvements.</li> <li value="7">Partner with Product and Engineering leadership on platform roadmap decisions and investment trade-offs.</li> <li value="8">Mentor Senior and Intermediate engineers, reduce technical debt, build reusable patterns that improve team throughput, and lead adoption of artificial intelligence-assisted and agentic workflows with quality, security, privacy, and operational guardrails.</li> </ul> <h2>What you’ll bring</h2> <ul> <li value="1">A record of leading technical work across more than one team or a broad product area.</li> <li value="2">Deep backend architecture and production experience with complex applications, services, or platforms, including application programming interfaces, service platforms, data systems, modular monoliths, or shared backend components.</li> <li value="3">Experience title: Staff Backend Engineer, Database Automation (Go)
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2>An overview of this role</h2> <p>As a Senior or Staff Backend Engineer with the <a class="textLink" href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/data-engineering/database-excellence/">Database Excellence group</a>, you'll build and evolve database automation and PostgreSQL as a service capabilities for GitLab. The level will be determined during the hiring process. You'll use Go to automate the full lifecycle of PostgreSQL across GitLab's infrastructure, making database operations safer, more consistent, and easier to scale for databases that sit behind high-throughput, always-on internet services. You'll work closely with partner teams to shape how GitLab provisions and manages PostgreSQL in a fully remote, highly collaborative environment.</p> <p>Some examples of our projects:</p> <ul> <li value="1"><a class="textLink" href="https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/database-team/traffic-replay-poc">SQL Traffic Replay Tooling</a>, which validates upgrades and changes against real production workloads.</li> <li value="2"><a class="textLink" href="https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-org/database-team/backend/-/work_items/1">PostgreSQL as a Service Platform</a>, which provides standardized, automated provisioning and lifecycle management for internal product databases.</li> <li value="3"><a class="textLink" href="https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-com/gl-infra/data-access/dbo/-/work_items/75">PostgreSQL Major Version Upgrade Automation</a>, which supports safe, repeatable major upgrades at GitLab.com scale.</li> </ul> <h2>What you’ll do</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Design, build, and maintain Go-based automation that manages the full PostgreSQL lifecycle, including provisioning, configuration, upgrades, failover, scaling, and decommissioning, reducing reactive operational work that currently takes more than 80% of the team's time.</li> <li value="2">Build automation that works across infrastructure-as-code tooling and cloud infrastructure, and evaluate operator-based approaches as the platform evolves.</li> <li value="3">Use AI agents as a regular part of building and operating services, including implementation, review, and reducing repetitive work, while keeping the context agents need in the repository so the whole team can build on it.</li> <li value="4">Build for internet scale by designing automation and services for high-throughput, always-on production workloads, where GitLab.com traffic sets the bar for correctness, latency, and availability.</li> <li value="5">Integrate compute, storage, networking, identity and access management, and managed data services across cloud providers into one coherent PostgreSQL platform instead of creating bespoke setups for each database.</li> <li value="6">Build GitLab's PostgreSQL as a service platform to replace bespoke database setups with standardized, automated provisioning and lifecycle management, so supporting more databases doesn't require growing the operations team at the same rate.</li> <li value="7">Collaborate closely with product management, infrastructure, software delivery, and other engineering teams to design and ship high-performing solutions.</li> <li value="8">Research, design, and implement improvements to PostgreSQL performance, scalability, and data health, helping maintain more than 8 months of operational runway for all critical database saturation points.</li> <li value="9">Review database automation and Go changes from other engineers and contributors, with attention to safety, maintainability, and performance.</li> <li value="10">Document automation practices, PostgreSQL operational patterns, and guidance that helps engineers use and contribute to the platform.</li> <li value="11">Build safe, repeatable automation for PostgreSQL major version upgrades at GitLab.com scale, validating changes against real production traffic before rollout.</li> <li value="12">Operate what you build in production from end to end, using production feedback to guide each iteration.</li> </ul> <h2>What you’ll bring</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Professional software engineering experience working with PostgreSQL in large, complex production environments, including experience building or operating a database-as-a-service product.</li> <li value="2">Proficiency with Go, including designing, implementing, testing, and reviewing backend services.</li> <li value="3">Experience developing Kubernetes operators, controllers, or similar automation for the lifecycle of stateful services, especially databases. Kubernetes experience is one way to demonstrate this skill, but isn't required; comparable experience building database or infrastructure automation is welcome.</li> <li value="4">Comfort with infrastructure as code and core database operations concepts such as high availability, replication, backups, and system-level performance trade-offs.</li> <li value="5">Familiarity with Ruby is a plus but isn't required. Much of GitLab's application codebase uses Ruby on Rails, and being able to read it helps when designing automation that application teams depend on. We’ll expect you to become comfortable with it on the job, not on day one.</li> <li value="6">Strong written communication skills and comfort working asynchronously in an all-remote, distributed team.</li> <li value="7">Self-directed work style with effective organizational skills, the ability to manage priorities as a "manager of one," and alignment with GitLab's values of transparency, collaboration, inclusion, and open source contribution, as well as its <a class="textLink" href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/company/operating-principles/">operating principles</a>.</li> <li value="8">Ownership of the technical direction for a major initiative such as the PostgreSQL as a service platform, turning an ambiguous problem into an architecture and a sequenced plan that several engineers can execute in parallel.</li> <li value="9">Influence beyond the team, setting the patterns other engineers follow, partnering with sibling database, infrastructure, and platform teams, and growing engineers through design reviews and mentorship.</li> </ul> <h2>About the team</h2> <p>The <a class="textLink" href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/data-engineering/database-excellence/">Database Excellence group</a> keeps GitLab’s databases running reliably through proactive health management, operational excellence, and strategic enablement. We maintain operational runway by identifying and addressing saturation points, operate infrastructure through automated and scalable processes, and provide tools and frameworks that help teams build features sustainably. Our primary focus is GitLab.com, and we're expanding our scope to provide database health frameworks and tooling that benefit self-managed customers as well.</p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. projects</strong></h3> <ul> <li> <div><strong>Project Examples</strong><br>In this role, you may lead projects such as:</div> <ul> <li><strong>Internal developer platform adoption:</strong> Build and environments:</strong> Build development, CI, and test environments that reflect production Kubernetes behavior — including third-party operators and the custom resources services depend on — sequencing CRD establishment, controller readiness, and dependent workloads so engineers get a working environment rather than a partially reconciled one, across both local and remote clusters.</li> <li><strong>Platform reliability and observability:</strong> Partner with infrastructure and service teams to improve rollout safety, troubleshooting, service health, resource management, and operational visibility across Kubernetes workloads.</li> </ul> <div><strong>What You'll Do</strong></div> <ul> <li>Lead and grow a team responsible for developer tooling and internal platform capabilities used by engineering teams to build and operate services.</li> <li>Set and execute a roadmap for Kubernetes-based developer workflows, balancing developer experience, platform reliability, security, and operational efficiency.</li> <li>Guide the design of reusable onboarding and deployment patterns for services running on Kubernetes, including workloads, networking, configuration and secrets, identity, storage, observability, progressive delivery, and the custom resources and controllers that services depend on.</li> <li>Make environment bring-up and teardown deterministic — resolving readiness and ordering dependencies between CRDs, controllers, and the workloads that rely on them — so engineers get reproducible environments instead of intermittent failures.</li> <li>Partner with infrastructure, security, and application teams to turn Kubernetes capabilities into simple, well-supported workflows rather than requiring every service team to become a Kubernetes expert.</li> <li>Establish engineering standards, documentation, automation, and feedback loops that improve adoption and reduce the time required to bring a service from development to production.</li> <li>Coach engineers through architectural decisions, incident follow-up, and production operations while maintaining a clear focus on sustainable team delivery.</li> <li>Represent the team with technical and organizational stakeholders, communicate tradeoffs clearly, and use adoption and reliability measures to guide prioritization.</li> </ul> <div><strong>What You'll implementing, testing, and operating production-quality services, command-line tools, automation, or platform tooling. Experience contributing to Ruby-based systems is also valuable for this role.</li> <li>Practical Kubernetes experience building or operating production workloads and platform capabilities, including deployments, services, networking, configuration and secrets, observability, resource management, and troubleshooting.</li> <li><strong>Depth in Kubernetes deployment lifecycle: Helm-based deployment and release management, kubeconfig and multi-cluster context handling including deploying into clusters you don't own, and integrating third-party operators and their custom resources (CloudNativePG, cert-manager and similar) into working environments — including the readiness and ordering problems that come with them: waiting on CRD establishment, controller availability, and custom resources reaching their own definition of ready. title: Staff Commercial Pricing Strategist
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h2> <p>The Pricing Strategy team owns the end-to-end pricing, packaging, and commercialization strategy across GitLab's product portfolio, from Premium and Ultimate tiers to GitLab Duo and our expanding artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities. As a Staff-level pricing and commercialization expert, you'll design, scale, and drive GitLab's enterprise monetization and commercial buying programs as an individual contributor at the top of our individual contributor track. You'll serve as the architect of our Enterprise Agreements, cloud marketplace and channel pricing structures, and competitive commercial programs, partnering across Product, go-to-market (GTM), Finance, Sales, Renewals, Product Marketing, Partners, and Deal Desk to turn pricing decisions into scalable programs that work for customers and the field.</p> <h2><strong>What you'll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Drive competitive pricing programs and tactical deal plays, including promotions, competitive replacement offers, and deal support, that help the field win and displace competitors in the DevSecOps and AI tooling market.</li> <li>Own list-to-net price realization strategy across products, geographic regions, GTM segments, and routes to market.</li> <li>Partner with Product Management, Product Marketing, and GTM leaders to shape new packaging and pricing proposals, evaluate monetization models as GitLab's AI and platform capabilities evolve, and bring data-backed recommendations to cross-functional and executive stakeholders.</li> <li>Act as the go-to expert for pricing enablement by building training, playbooks, and battlecards that give the field confidence in pricing conversations and help them explain commercial value.</li> <li>Put commercial programs into practice in partnership with Deal Desk, Revenue Operations, and Data teams, staying hands-on with execution as well as strategy.</li> <li>Define, launch, and scale Enterprise Agreements and marketed bundling strategies that simplify transactions, encourage multi-product and GitLab Duo adoption, and maximize customer lifetime value.</li> <li>Define channel and marketplace pricing strategy, including tiering, discounting frameworks, and margin structures, across resellers, global systems integrators, independent software vendors, and cloud marketplaces such as Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud Platform, and Microsoft Azure.</li> <li>Document decisions and frameworks in the GitLab handbook and default to asynchronous, written communication as part of GitLab's all-remote, globally distributed team.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Extensive experience across strategy consulting, pricing, strategic finance, or corporate or deal strategy, ideally at a software as a service or enterprise software company.</li> <li>Deep experience in monetization or pricing strategy, including direct ownership of pricing waterfalls, enterprise buying programs such as Enterprise License Agreements or Enterprise Agreements, or channel and marketplace pricing models.</li> <li>A track record of operating as a go-to expert without formal authority. You won't just support our people systems, you'll build them: owning the code, pipelines, and integrations that keep GitLab's People automation ecosystem running reliably at scale across Workato, Google Cloud, Claude, Workday, and the tools that power our global workforce. This is a strong fit if you think like a software engineer first, write clean and maintainable code, and thrive at the intersection of people systems, AI, innovation, and automation engineering.</p> <p>In this role, you'll be the technical backbone of our People Technology team, designing, building, and maintaining the automations, agents, and integrations that connect Workday, Greenhouse, Slack, and internal tools. You'll be the go-to technical thought partner for the people group on complex engineering decisions, and your work will compound over time: fewer manual processes, stronger system reliability, and a People technology foundation that scales without friction.</p> <p><strong>What You’ll Do</strong>  </p> <ul> <li>Own the design, development, and maintenance of people system automations and integrations across Workato, Google Cloud Platform, Claude, Workday, Greenhouse and GitLab, writing reliable, well-tested code that runs at scale.</li> <li>Build and maintain integrations between Workday, Greenhouse, Slack, and internal tools using Workday Web Services (WWS) and Slack's API and Bot SDK, diagnosing failures proactively and driving uptime and reliability improvements across the automation stack.</li> <li>Write, version, and maintain automation code in Ruby (or comparable scripting languages) stored in GitLab, with clear documentation, code reviews, and disciplined change management practices.</li> <li>Develop and manage Slack apps and bots that deliver intuitive, automated workflows, reducing friction for People teams and employees across a globally distributed workforce.</li> <li>Move past surface-level requests to diagnose root problems, challenge assumptions, and co-design automation solutions that are durable, scalable, and built to last.</li> <li>Serve as subject matter expert on Workato automation architecture, driving standardization, reusability, and scalability across the People technology integration layer.</li> <li>Maintain and improve CI/CD pipelines and deployment practices for People system automation, ensuring changes are tested, reviewed, and safely deployed using GitLab.</li> <li>Leverage AI tools, large language models (LLMs), and Model Context Protocol (MCP) frameworks, including Claude, to accelerate automation development and identify opportunities to eliminate manual work across the People Group.</li> <li>Provide technical guidance to teammates and stakeholders, proactively communicating context and decision-making, partnering closely with InfoSec, AI Engineering, and IT, and raising the bar for how automations, agents, and integrations are built, documented, and maintained.</li> <li>Exercise independent judgment on methods and evaluation criteria to obtain quality results, leading others by sharing solutions and problem-solving approaches.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What You’ll Bring </strong></p> <ul> <li>Hands-on experience writing and maintaining code in Ruby or a comparable scripting language (Python, PHP, etc.), you're comfortable in a codebase, write code others can read and maintain, and are willing to learn Ruby if you haven't already.</li> <li>Deep expertise in Workato or a comparable enterprise automation/integration platform, with a track record of building reliable, scalable automation workflows in production environments.</li> <li>Strong experience integrating with Workday using Workday Web Services (WWS), with the instinct to build integrations that are durable, observable, and handle edge cases well.</li> <li>Experience building Slack apps and automations using Slack's API and Bot SDK, with an eye for delivering workflows that actually get used.</li> <li>Proficiency with Git and GitLab for version control, code review, and CI/CD workflows, you treat automation code like production software, not scripts on someone's laptop.</li> <li>Familiarity with Google Cloud Platform (GCP) or AWS; experience with Docker and Kubernetes (GKE is a bonus) for running and maintaining automation services.</li> <li>Experience connecting HR systems including Workday, Greenhouse, and internal tools, with strong instincts for where integration points break and how to keep them reliable.</li> <li>Comfort working with AI tools and MCP frameworks to accelerate development, automate repetitive work, and push the boundaries of what people technology can do.</li> <li>Strong communication skills, you can translate technical architecture into clear decisions and stakeholder updates, and you know when to surface a risk versus just fix it.</li> <li>An engineering mindset applied to people systems: you treat reliability, observability, and maintainability as first-class concerns, not afterthoughts.</li> <li>People system fluency, you understand how HR data flows, why it matters, and how to build automations that handle it with care and accuracy.</li> <li>Intellectual curiosity and a bias for action, you don't wait to be told what's brittle; you find it, frame the fix, and drive it forward.</li> </ul> <p><strong>About the team</strong></p> <p>The People Technology team is building the systems foundation that allows GitLab to scale as a global, all-remote company. We don't just keep the lights on, we push the bar on what people technology can do, constantly improving reliability, usability, and intelligence across the platforms that power our People organization. We work across core systems, integrations, automation, and compliance, partnering closely with stakeholders across time zones to move fast, build with purpose, and create an experience where technology enables people to do their best work.</p> <h4><strong>How GitLab will support you</strong></h4> <ul> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/" target="_blank">Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/paid-time-off/" target="_blank">Flexible Paid Time Off</a> </li> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/company/culture/inclusion/erg-guide/#:~:text=Definition%20of%20the%20TMRG%20%2D%20Team%20Member%20Resource%20Groups,-TMRGs%20are%20voluntary&text=The%20purpose%20for%20this%20type,developing%20the%20sense%20of%20belonging." target="_blank">Team Member Resource Groups</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/stock-options/" target="_blank">Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/learning-and-development/growth-and-development/" target="_blank">Growth and Development Fund</a></li> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/#parental-leave" target="_blank">Parental leave</a> </li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/finance/expenses/#equipment" target="_blank">Home office</a> support</li> </ul> <p>Please note that we welcome interest from candidates with varying levels of experience; many successful candidates do not meet every single requirement. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h2> <p>As a Staff Enterprise Architect, you will design and evolve how GitLab's internal systems are configured, integrate, perform and scale to support a rapidly growing business. Reporting to the Director, Enterprise Architecture and AI Intelligent Automation, you will apply all four architecture lenses (business, application, data, and technology) to the systems in your scope, treating AI as a standing consideration inside each rather than a separate workstream.</p> <p>Enterprise-wide strategy, portfolio direction, and standards ownership sit with the Director. Your job is depth: turning that direction into designs detailed enough to build, and being the person trusted with the hardest technical problems in the enterprise. You will not manage people. You will lead through architecture, as the partner to our Applications engineering teams and to Integration, RPA, and Intelligent Automation, and as a reviewer on the Architecture Review Board, where the aim is to make architecture an enabler rather than a gate.</p> <h2><strong>What you'll do</strong></h2> <p><strong>Business architecture</strong></p> <ul> <li>In collaboration with product management and process owners, map the current-state processes and capabilities supported by the systems in your scope, tying each capability to its supporting systems, owners, and systems of record, and identify and resolve where those systems create friction, manual handoffs, or duplicated work, including handoffs an AI agent could remove entirely.</li> <li>Architect end-to-end processes that span front-office and back-office systems, including new product introduction, CPQ and quote-to-cash, billing and revenue recognition, renewals, and record-to-report, together with the customer service processes that run alongside them, including case and escalation management, entitlements, and service level commitments, rather than optimizing any one system in isolation.</li> <li>Redesign workflows before automating them, so we aren't encoding broken processes into new tooling. For each step, decide what an AI agent should handle, what deterministic automation should handle, and what stays with a person.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Application architecture</strong></p> <ul> <li>In collaboration with the Applications engineering teams, serve as their embedded architect, producing high level designs and patterns for changes to Salesforce, NetSuite, Zuora, Zendesk, and other core platforms. Favor configuration and supported extension patterns over customization, evaluate each platform's native AI before anything bespoke is built, and keep system roadmaps aligned with enterprise standards.</li> <li>Design for maintainability and supportability: clear service ownership, observability and error handling in integrations, documented runbooks, and realistic total cost of ownership.</li> <li>Go deep on the platforms in your scope, staying current on release notes, published limits, API behavior, and known constraints, so designs account for what the platform will actually do rather than what the documentation promises.</li> <li>Govern application change by reviewing significant build proposals, data model changes, and third-party package additions before they are committed, giving teams a clear and timely decision, and keeping platforms on supported versions and ready to upgrade.</li> <li>In collaboration with each domain's technical lead, or the vendor where that is the better source, run quarterly health checks on Salesforce, NetSuite, Zuora, Zendesk, and Workato, measuring customization footprint against each platform's published ceilings for API and governor limits, automation, storage, transaction and ticket volumes, AI consumption, and licenses. Publish a report card showing headroom, what is trending toward a limit, and who owns the fix.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Data architecture</strong></p> <ul> <li>Architect data flows across operational and analytical planes, including the retrieval and grounding patterns that make enterprise data usable by AI, alongside API-first integrations, event-driven patterns, batch pipelines, data warehouse models, and reverse ETL back into business systems.</li> <li>Design data access and handling patterns that meet privacy, residency, and SOX requirements, setting explicit boundaries on what AI models and agents may read, retain, or act on, plus field-level controls for sensitive customer and financial data.</li> <li>Establish integration and data contracts between systems, so downstream consumers aren't adversely affected by upstream schema changes.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Technology architecture</strong></p> <ul> <li>Define platform and integration patterns for the systems in your scope, spanning iPaaS (Workato), identity and access management, secrets handling, and the cloud services those systems depend on. Define how each system exposes its capability to AI agents, through APIs, tool interfaces, and scoped permissions.</li> <li>In collaboration with Infrastructure, design for reliability and scale, covering environment strategy, sandbox and test data management, and non-functional requirements, while CI/CD and disaster recovery remain theirs to own.</li> <li>In collaboration with Security, design authentication, authorization, and service-to-service access for the systems in your scope, applying the standards they and the Director set.</li> <li>In collaboration with the enterprise AI team, recommend, use case by use case, whether a need is best served by domain-specific AI embedded in a business application or by a shared enterprise AI capability, applying their decision and model governance framework, and assemble the evidence each recommendation rests on: data access and sensitivity, reuse across functions, and cost.</li> <li>Monitor and optimize cloud and platform consumption, covering right-sizing, license and API-limit management, and eliminating spend on unused or duplicated capacity.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Across all four domains</strong></p> <ul> <li>Produce the designs teams build from: target-state architectures, decision records, reference patterns, and high level designs for major projects and significant platform changes. Specify them in enough detail to build against: data models, field-level mappings, error and retry behavior, failure modes, and how AI output is evaluated where a design uses it. Every design must satisfy SOX, internal control, and security requirements.</li> <li>Co-author those designs with engineering teams and stay with them through build, making the call on trade-offs, resolving ambiguity in the spec, and unblocking decisions so delivery doesn't stall.</li> <li>Take the hardest technical problems in your domains personally, building proofs of concept when a decision cannot be settled on paper, including the production issues no one else has been able to root-cause.</li> <li>Collaborate very closely with adjacent technology teams, including Data, Security, and Infrastructure, so that architecture is thought through end to end and serves the whole enterprise rather than one function at a time.</li> <li>Maintain a prioritized inventory of technical debt across your domains and drive it down by attaching remediation to funded projects, upgrades, and migrations already touching that surface. Root-cause production defects rather than clearing them, fixing the design so the same class of defect stops recurring.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Deep expertise in application architecture and data architecture, with working fluency in business process and technology architecture, AI as a working lens across all four, and the judgment to know which lens a given problem needs.</li> <li>Strong hands-on background in integration, automation, and applied AI, including retrieval-augmented generation, tool calling and agent orchestration on a platform such as Claude, plus the evaluation and guardrails that make them safe to deploy, the judgment to know where AI belongs and where it does not, and fluency using AI in your own daily work, including AI-assisted development, rather than only designing it for others.</li> <li>Hands-on experience architecting core business systems, including ERP, CRM, CPQ, billing, financial, and customer service platforms, with the discipline to keep them standard, upgradeable, and SOX-compliant, plus fluency in the processes that cross them, from quote-to-cash through record-to-report.</li> <li>Expert-level knowledge of data modeling, integration architecture patterns, and API design for enterprise systems, plus practical experience with data warehouse technologies and ELT, ETL and reverse ETL pipelines, across operational and analytical use cases.</li> <li>Depth in iPaaS tooling and the operational realities of running integrations in production, including cost and consumption optimization, plus working knowledge of the cloud platforms those integrations run on.</li> <li>A track record of driving architectural change through influence rather than authority: designs that survived implementation, standards adopted on platforms owned by other teams, a clear technical position held in review forums without losing the partnership, and trade-offs explained in plain business language to Director and VP stakeholders, in writing and async.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>The Enterprise Architecture team at GitLab designs, governs, and evolves the internal technology landscape that powers our business. We build with Claude across our enterprise systems, from agent-assisted workflows in our core platforms to the tooling our own team uses daily. You’ll help set the technical direction for a unified purchase flow, mentor other engineers, and partner with Product, Design, Billing, and Support to improve how customers buy and grow with GitLab. This role reports to the Engineering Manager, Purchase.</p> <p><strong><strong class="textBold">Some examples of our projects:</strong></strong></p> <ul> <li value="1">Unifying separate purchase flows into one consistent purchase experience</li> <li value="2">Building and scaling GitLab Flex subscription flows that let customers reserve spend month to month across seats, artificial intelligence (AI) credits, Runners, and other GitLab capabilities without renegotiating their contract</li> <li value="3">Evolving self-service promotional discounts for existing and prospective customers</li> <li value="4">Modernizing the purchase frontend to improve clarity, accessibility, and conversion</li> <li value="5">Strengthening integrations between the purchase flow and downstream billing and CRM systems for accuracy and resilience</li> </ul> <h2>What you’ll do</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Design and build fullstack features across the purchase journey.</li> <li value="2">Lead technical design for new purchasing capabilities and the unified purchase experience.</li> <li value="3">Partner with Product and Design to turn purchasing requirements into resilient, well-tested technical solutions.</li> <li value="4">Ensure purchase flows integrate correctly and safely with downstream billing and CRM systems.</li> <li value="5">Set and uphold engineering standards for code quality, testing, rollout safety, and monitoring.</li> <li value="6">Mentor engineers and review merge requests with thoughtful, constructive feedback.</li> <li value="7">Identify and reduce technical debt and architectural risk in the purchase experience.</li> <li value="8">Participate in incident response for purchase-related issues because of their direct revenue impact.</li> </ul> <h2>What you’ll bring</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Professional fullstack engineering experience across frontend and backend code; title: Staff Product Manager, Agentic Test Intelligence
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h2> <p>As Staff Product Manager, Test & Code Coverage, you'll build product capabilities from initial discovery through launch and adoption. You'll help engineering teams understand why pipelines fail, improve test automation, and use code coverage to make better decisions about software quality and risk.</p> <p>You'll turn a technically complex problem space into a focused strategy, roadmap, and developer experience. Working closely with Engineering and Design, you'll explore how agents can diagnose failures, recommend next steps, and help teams recover safely. The goal isn't to add artificial intelligence (AI) for its own sake. It's to reduce manual work and help developers get back to a safe, shippable state without losing trust or control.</p> <p>At GitLab, our mission is simple: to enable everyone to contribute to and co-create the software that powers our world. You'll contribute to that mission by making testing and coverage insights more useful across the software development lifecycle.</p> <h2><strong>What you'll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Define and communicate the Test & Code Coverage product vision, strategy, and outcome-focused roadmap, from discovery through a minimum viable product, beta, launch, and continued iteration.</li> <li>Identify customer problems across pipeline failure diagnosis, test automation, test optimization, code coverage, and recovery. Build the case for investment, prioritize foundational and customer-facing work, and reshape or stop initiatives that aren't creating value.</li> <li>Work with Engineering to understand pipeline failures caused by flaky tests, testing gaps, environment issues, configuration problems, and coverage blind spots. Connect code changes, tests, pipeline behavior, historical patterns, and risk to help developers find a diagnosis and an actionable next step.</li> <li>Work directly with customers to understand how they author, maintain, select, prioritize, and debug tests. Connect test selection, test impact analysis, code coverage, and pipeline intelligence to reduce flaky tests, shorten feedback loops, and focus testing effort where it lowers the most risk.</li> <li>Partner with Engineering and Design to prototype agent-driven workflows for failure diagnosis, test authoring and repair, optimization, coverage analysis, and recovery. Make actions reviewable through evidence, confidence, human approval, and safe paths to propose code changes and merge requests. Use AI tools in your own product work to investigate problems, explore code and data, prototype concepts, and accelerate learning.</li> <li>Define and measure outcomes such as time to diagnose, time to recover, failure recurrence, test signal quality, and developer confidence. Validate problems and solutions with customers and learn from production usage.</li> <li>Partner across Product, Engineering, Design, Quality, Developer Experience, Customer Success, Support, and Product Marketing to connect testing insights with code review, pipelines, and release decisions. Turn customer evidence into clear narratives that support adoption and future investment.</li> <li>Lead through clear written communication, prioritization, and product judgment. Influence senior stakeholders, establish repeatable discovery and measurement practices, and mentor other product managers.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Experience owning complex technical products, platforms, or developer workflows at Staff, Senior Staff, Principal, or equivalent scope, including building a new product or capability from initial validation through launch and adoption.</li> <li>Strong product fundamentals in customer discovery, problem framing, prioritization, roadmap development, outcome measurement, and iterative delivery.</li> <li>Technical fluency in one or more relevant areas, such as software testing, test automation, code coverage, continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), developer tools, DevOps, developer experience, quality engineering, or software delivery.</li> <li>An understanding of how engineering teams build, test, review, and ship software, and the ability to work with engineers on test architecture, pipeline behavior, code changes, data, integrations, reliability, and scale.</li> <li>Experience diagnosing technical problems and turning complex, noisy signals into clear user experiences and actionable workflows.</li> <li>Experience exploring AI or agent-driven solutions for developer workflows, with the judgment to distinguish useful automation from unsafe or low-confidence actions.</li> <li>Experience using customer conversations to understand problems and inform product decisions, communicating clearly in writing and conversation, and influencing across functions with shared ownership. You can work directly with developers, quality engineers, platform teams, engineering leaders, and executives, and move between strategy and implementation detail.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>Our work brings together Product, Engineering, and Design, with input from Quality, Developer Experience, Customer Success, Support, and Product Marketing. We work directly with developers, quality engineers, and engineering leaders to understand their testing practices, validate ideas, and learn from how they use the product.</p> <p>We give Engineering and Design clear customer context and room to shape solutions. Our decisions draw on customer evidence and measurable outcomes, and we revisit approaches that aren't creating value. You'll contribute to how we discover problems, prioritize work, and measure progress, as well as sharing product management practices with other product managers.</p> <p>As part of GitLab's all-remote organization, we collaborate asynchronously across regions. Our work emphasizes transparency, written communication, and clear decision-making.</p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. Requirements Translation</strong></p> <ul> <li>Serve as the primary internal product voice for all QTC and Finance Systems initiatives, partnering closely with Finance, Accounting, Revenue Operations, Deal Desk, and Legal.</li> <li>Lead discovery, requirements workshops, and business process design sessions to translate complex financial and commercial requirements into actionable system criteria definition, and roadmap communication.</li> <li>Model and instill product management best practices—user story writing, prioritization frameworks (e.g., RICE, MoSCoW), sprint review how ETA delivers business value.</li> <li>Provide structured feedback and growth coaching to BSAs on career development, helping analysts grow toward senior and lead levels.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Program Strategy & Delivery Oversight</strong></p> <ul> <li>Lead product strategy for major multi-quarter programs (e.g., consumption-based billing iterations, CLM/Order Forms, Zuora Product Catalog refactors, ERP optimization) from discovery through go-live.</li> <li>Define and maintain program-level dependency maps across concurrent workstreams, surfacing risks early and driving cross-team resolution.</li> <li>Own UAT strategy and acceptance criteria in collaboration with BSAs, ensuring system changes meet business requirements before production release.</li> <li>Support post-launch stabilization and continuous improvement cycles, prioritizing defect resolution and incremental enhancements based on business impact.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Systems Architecture Collaboration</strong></p> <ul> <li>Partner with Enterprise Architects and Engineering Managers to evaluate build-vs-buy-vs-configure decisions for new capabilities.</li> <li>Bring informed opinions on QTC platform architecture trade-offs (e.g., billing model design, middleware integration patterns, revenue recognition rule configuration) based on deep domain knowledge.</li> <li>Stay current on platform roadmaps for Salesforce, Zuora, and NetSuite, identifying opportunities to leverage native capabilities before custom builds.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>What You’ll Bring </strong></h3> <ul> Quote-to-Cash systems: Salesforce CPQ, Zuora Billing, Zuora Revenue, and NetSuite ERP are the core stack—hands-on configuration or implementation experience strongly preferred.</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to own and communicate multi-quarter internal product roadmaps to senior business and technology stakeholders.</li> <li>Strong command of revenue lifecycle processes: opportunity-to-quote, order management, billing and collections, revenue recognition (ASC 606), and financial close.</li> <li>Experience operating in a SOX-controlled environment with an understanding of audit trails, approval workflows, and change management requirements for financial systems.</li> <li>Track record of successfully running complex, multi-program delivery environments with competing priorities and shared engineering resources.</li> <li>Sufficient technical fluency to engage meaningfully with engineering on API design, data model decisions, and integration trade-offs—without needing to write code.</li> <li>Experience with consumption-based or usage-based billing models</li> </ul> <p> </p> <h3><strong>About the team</strong></h3> <p>You'll be joining the Revenue Lifecycle & Finance Systems Our mission is to embed proactive guidance directly into modern developer workflows and automated coding environments, embedding security standards into the software development process from the outset. We strive to enable teams to deliver secure, resilient software seamlessly while minimizing reliance on manual security gates.</p> <p>In this role, you will collaborate closely with product engineering organizations, spearhead architectural strategy for critical capabilities, and serve as the primary Security Owner driving risk reduction for key entries within our risk management framework. do</strong>  </p> <ul> <li>Partner with engineering and product leadership across GitLab, developing enough context in their domains to anticipate security problems rather than react to them</li> and prototypes to unblock engineering teams and shorten the distance between a security requirement and a working implementation</li> <li>Conduct security architecture reviews for large or strategic projects, and coordinate with Application Security so that review coverage is comprehensive and correctly prioritised</li> <li>Threat model new and existing systems, and establish the patterns that let teams threat model their own work</li> <li>Work with Security Research on proactive exploration of unknown risks in GitLab's architecture</li> <li>Anticipate emerging security challenges and propose architectural responses before they reach implementation</li> <li>Mentor security engineers across the division, and represent security architecture to engineering audiences</li> </ul> <p><strong>What you’ll bring </strong></p> <ul> <li>Depth in application security architecture, including authentication and authorization models, privilege escalation, multi-tenant isolation, and trust boundary analysis</li> <li>Experience securing distributed systems, including service-to-service authentication, secrets handling, and the failure modes of security decisions made across process boundaries</li> <li>Working knowledge of software supply chain security: build and release integrity, artifact provenance, and dependency risk</li> <li>A track record of proactive architecture work — identifying risk before it becomes an incident, and designing something that prevents a class of problem rather than an instance of one</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to build trusted relationships with engineering leadership and influence technical direction through expertise rather than gatekeeping</li> <li>Experience defining security standards or patterns that teams adopted without being compelled to</li> <li>The ability to operate strategically while remaining hands-on, including reading unfamiliar code, building prototypes, and contributing changes</li> <li>Clear written communication, and the ability to make a security argument to an engineering audience that does not already agree with it</li> <li>A view on how security guidance should be authored and delivered for AI coding tools, not only for humans</li> </ul> <p><strong>About the team</strong></p> <p>Security Architects are a part of our <a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/security/product-security/security-platforms-architecture/">Security Platforms and Architecture</a> team, who address complex security challenges facing GitLab and its customers to enable GitLab to be the most secure software factory platform on the market. Composed of <a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/security/product-security/security-platforms-architecture/security-architecture/">Security Architecture</a>, <a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/security/product-security/security-platforms-architecture/security-research/">Security Research</a>, and Application Security, we focus on systemic product security risks and work cross-functionally to mitigate them while maintaining Engineering’s development velocity.</p> <p>In FY27, we're implementing a new organizational model where each architect is dedicated to a specific functional area of GitLab's product, enabling deeper context, stronger relationships, and more proactive security guidance. As the Core DevOps architect, you'll be part of a team that includes architects focused on AI and the Sec Section, creating opportunities for collaboration on cross-cutting security challenges while maintaining specialized expertise in your domain.</p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. Requests may include user migrations, de-duplication, Renewal Manager ownership changes, compensation exceptions, and Salesforce or data issues.</li> <li>Raise the operating standard in your domain by documenting processes, mentoring others on how the renewal motion works, and contributing to broader Revenue Operations initiatives that need the renewals perspective.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Experience in Renewals Operations, Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, management consulting, strategy, or a similar analytical and problem-solving role, with ownership of operational improvements and cross-functional initiatives.</li> <li>Hands-on experience with both consumption and subscription renewal motions, including renewal forecasting, retention reporting, and the contractual and process mechanics that govern how renewals close.</li> <li>Strong critical thinking and structured problem-solving skills. You can break down ambiguous problems into clear workstreams and move them forward.</li> <li>Strong quantitative and analytical skills. You're highly proficient in Excel or Google Sheets, can build and validate models from scratch, and can translate analysis into clear recommendations and action. Experience with Structured Query Language (SQL) or equivalent data-querying tools is preferred, not required.</li> <li>Systems thinking and experience using Salesforce for pipeline and renewals reporting. You understand how changes in one part of the go-to-market motion affect others, including how CRM, subscription or entitlement records, quoting, and billing relate to one another, and you design solutions accordingly.</li> <li>Sound commercial judgment and an understanding of renewal complexity, including co-terming, amendments, expansions, downgrades, price changes, multiyear agreements, auto-renewals, procurement requirements, and approval policies.</li> <li>Strong cross-functional collaboration skills. These partnerships connect renewal execution with the processes, systems, and data that support it. In GitLab's all-remote, values-driven environment, documentation, iteration, and cross-functional partnership are core to how you'll work.</p> <p><br><br></p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h4><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h4> <p>As a Staff Security Governance Engineer, you will be the individual contributor who owns how GitLab writes, maintains, communicates, and measures its security policies and standards. You will turn emerging regulations, including AI regulation, into clear requirements that engineering, product, and legal teams can act on, and you will use automation to keep governance lightweight and continuous rather than a point-in-time exercise. You will sit on the Security Governance team within Security Assurance and work closely with Security Compliance, Security Risk, and GRC Engineering. You will report to the Director, Customer Trust & Security Governance.</p> <h4><strong>What you'll do</strong></h4> <ul> <li><em>Policies and standards</em></li> <ul> <li>Own the end-to-end lifecycle of GitLab's security policies, standards, procedures, and guidelines: drafting, stakeholder review, approval, publication, annual review, and retirement.</li> <li>Define and run the exception management process, including risk-based approvals, expiry tracking, and trend reporting that shows where policies need to change.</li> <li>Run policy attestation and investigate non-adherence.</li> <li>Keep policies clear, practical, and aligned with how GitLab's engineering teams work in a DevSecOps environment.</li> </ul> <li><em>Regulatory and framework alignment</em></li> <ul> <li>Monitor emerging regulations and standards (e.g., EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001, sector or regional requirements) and partner with Legal well ahead of compliance deadlines to assess impact and update policy.</li> <li>Maintain mappings between our policies and frameworks such as SOC 2, ISO 27001, ISO 42001, FedRAMP, and NIST CSF, so requirements are written once and reused.</li> </ul> <li><em>Measurement and assurance</em></li> <ul> <li>Define KPIs for policy adherence and report trends to Security leadership.</li> <li>Run targeted internal assessments of adherence and drive remediation to closure.</li> <li>Support audit activities by coordinating evidence, testing, and remediation management.</li> </ul> <li><em>Customer trust</em></li> <ul> <li>Support customer questionnaires and customer meetings, and help turn recurring customer requests into better policies and self-service content.</li> </ul> <li><em>Automation and AI</em></li> <ul> <li>Identify and implement automation and AI-assisted workflows for policy management, evidence collection, control monitoring, and assessment work, in partnership with GRC Engineering.</li> </ul> <li><em>Technical leadership</em></li> <ul> <li>Act as a technical and program leader across Security, Product, Legal, and Engineering, influencing without direct authority.</li> <li>Mentor other team members and help set the direction of the Security Governance roadmap.</li> </ul> </ul> <h4><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h4> <ul> <li>10+ years in security governance, GRC, or IT risk, with hands-on ownership of a policy and standards lifecycle and measurable outcomes, ideally at a global technology company.</li> <li>Working knowledge of SOC 2, ISO 27001, ISO 42001, FedRAMP, and NIST CSF, including how to put them into practice, not only how to read them</li> <li>Experience creating and maintaining an enterprise Information Security Management System (ISMS), ideally including hands on involvement in ISO 27001 certification or recertification.<span class="screenreader-hidden-offscreen"> </span></li> <li>Understanding of cloud, SaaS, and DevSecOps practices, and the ability to write policy that engineers will follow.</li> <li>A risk-based mindset that balances compliance with real security risk.</li> <li>Demonstrated use of automation or AI to reduce manual GRC work.</li> <li>Strong written and verbal communication, including translating technical concepts for engineers, executives, auditors, and customers.</li> <li>Experience collaborating with Security, Product, Legal, and Engineering.</li> <li>Certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CISA, or similar are highly desirable.</li> </ul> <h4><strong>What success looks like</strong></h4> <ul> <li>First 30 days: Assessed the current policy library and exception process, built relationships with key stakeholders, and proposed a prioritized roadmap.</li> <li>First 90 days: Uplift the existing security policy library to align with NIST CSF, ISO 27001/27017/27018/42001, and PCI-DSS.</li> <li>First 120 days: A refreshed review cadence is in place, exception reporting is running, and can demonstrate a measurable improvement in policy adherence.</li> <li>First six months: Develop Policy as Code and collaborate with Security, Product, Legal, and Engineering for implementation into existing workflows.</li> </ul> <h4><strong>About the team</strong></h4> <p>The Security Assurance organization helps GitLab build and maintain trust by strengthening how we approach security, compliance, and risk. Security Governance sits within it and owns customer trust, security awareness, policies and standards, and other governance functions. Our counterparts are Security Compliance, Security Risk, and GRC Engineering. <br><br>You will join a small team of four direct reports under the Director, where each person has broad scope and visible impact. chained vulnerabilities in GitLab, where individual weaknesses combine for outsized impact.</li> <li>Validate security vulnerabilities through hands-on testing, developing proof-of-concept exploits than the instance.</li> <li>Conduct security research into GitLab's AI and agentic surfaces, and participate in defining the security requirements that engineering teams build against.</li> <li>Build dependencies integrated with GitLab, report findings to their maintainers, and track mitigation following our <a href="https://about.gitlab.com/security/disclosure/">responsible disclosure technical areas impacting the security of the product.</li> <li>Proficiency in one or more of Ruby, Go, Python, TypeScript, or Rust. Experience in AI frameworks is an asset.</li> <li>Ability to read and analyze code across multiple languages and codebases.</li> <li>Understanding of AI attack vectors including prompt injection, agent manipulation, and workflow exploitation</li> <li>Experience leading technical objectives in cross-functional teams</li> <li>Excellent written communication skills with an ability to articulate complex topics in a clear and concise manner.</li> <li>Ability to translate complex technical findings into clear risk assessments and remediation recommendations</li> <li>Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with creative thinking about attack scenarios</li> <li><strong>Nice to have: </strong>Published security research or conference presentations; Background in software engineering with distributed systems expertise; Security certifications such as OSCP, OSCE, GPEN, or similar; Experience with GitLab or similar DevSecOps platforms</li> </ul> <h4><strong>About the team</strong></h4> <p>Security Researchers are a part of our<a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/security/product-security/security-platforms-architecture/application-security/"> </a>Application Security team, who address complex security challenges facing GitLab and its customers to enable GitLab to be the most secure software factory platform on the market. description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h3><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h3> <p>As a Staff Backend Engineer on GitLab's Security Factory: Code Scanning team, you help developers find and fix security issues. Those issues live in the code they write, and you set the technical direction for the static analysis engine that finds them.</p> <p>Your work spans two complementary parts of a complete security analysis. On the engine side, you shape how the static analysis toolkit models a program: parsing source into intermediate representations, resolving symbols, building call graphs, and tracking tainted data across files and languages. You define the architecture and specifications the team builds against, and you delegate component specifications within them to engineers and to the AI agents that implement them. On the evaluation side, you build and apply tooling that tests, measures, and validates what the engine finds against benchmark applications with known vulnerabilities.</p> <p>What the engine can model and how we measure what it finds are parts of one picture. As a Staff engineer you hold that picture, shape the long-range technical goals of the team, and raise the bar for every engineer on it. We build the engine with AI agents that write and review code from written specifications, under human direction. We expect you to direct that work effectively and with good judgment, and to help the team do the same.</p> <h3><strong>What you do</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Act as the directly responsible individual (DRI) for the team's highest-scope initiatives from design through delivery, shipping large features with minimal guidance and shaping the long-range goals of the team</li> <li>Bring systems built by one engineer to team ownership through documentation, tests, and shared review</li> <li>Set the technical direction for the AI-assisted tooling that implements, reviews, and validates engine changes and findings, design the checks that decide whether an agent-written change or generated result is fit to merge, and measure detection quality against benchmark applications with known vulnerabilities, raising the bar for what counts as a trustworthy result. That includes static application security testing (SAST) rules mapped to CWE and OWASP, and the test fixtures that prove they work.</li> <li>Own the architecture of the program model (parsing, symbol resolution, intermediate representations, call graphs, and taint and data-flow analysis) and of the pipeline that turns source code into findings, and define how both extend to new languages and frameworks</li> <li>Solve technical problems of the highest scope and complexity, actively seek out difficult impediments affecting the whole team, and advocate for improvements to quality, security, and performance with Product Management, UX, and partner teams such as Code Security and Composition Analysis</li> <li>Mentor all engineers on the team through code review and pairing, remove blockers to their autonomy, and shepherd the definition and improvement of our internal standards through review</li> <li>Participate in on-call rotations to assist troubleshooting product operations, security operations, and urgent engineering issues</li> <li>Define the overarching architecture and specification documents for the engine, delegate component specifications within them, and drive their implementation by AI agents and engineers working independently through phased plans, small reviewable units of change, and specifications kept in lockstep with the code</li> <li>Build and maintain the harness, agent instructions, and agentic skills that keep agent-written code trustworthy, including separate coding and reviewing agents, rules and tests the coding agents cannot change, independent review panels of agents from different model providers, and performance, API, and dependency gates, with risky changes escalated to human review</li> <li>Stay current with research in program analysis and security, run AI-assisted research and spikes, and turn the findings into prototypes, proposals, and upstream contributions, including responsible disclosure of findings in open source projects</li> </ul> <h3><strong>What you bring</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Experience building your own LLM tooling, such as a harness, an agent pipeline, or evaluations, with the judgment to know when output is trustworthy and when it isn't</li> <li>Extensive professional experience writing, testing, and reviewing production code in Rust, Go, or a comparable systems language, with depth in at least one. The engine is Rust, the analyzer wrapper is Go, and the monolith integration is Ruby, and we value willingness to work across them.</li> <li>Experience with performance optimization and with containerized workflows and CI/CD (we use Docker heavily)</li> <li>A deep program analysis and static analysis background, such as parsing and ASTs, intermediate representations (SSA, control-flow and call graphs), taint and data-flow analysis, type inference, incremental and fixpoint computation, or writing detection rules, with the ability to read, evaluate, and apply the research literature</li> <li>Deep application security experience, such as vulnerability research, secure code review, or writing detection rules, and fluency with vulnerability classes (OWASP Top 10, CWE)</li> <li>Demonstrated capacity to communicate clearly and concisely about complex technical, architectural, and organizational problems, and to write architecture and design specifications that bring a team to a decision</li> <li>A track record of taking ownership of ambiguous, team-wide problems and shipping them from concept to production with minimal guidance, with specific, regular async updates on progress, blockers, risks, and next steps</li> <li>Experience defining a system's overarching architecture, delegating component specifications to engineers and AI agents, and getting them implemented reliably</li> <li>A track record of mentoring engineers, raising a team's technical bar, and influencing technical direction by achieving consensus with peers and leadership</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Helpful experience</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Familiarity with popular web or mobile application frameworks and how they handle input, data, and configuration</li> <li>Experience designing guardrails for agent-written code, such as mutation testing, fuzzing, and CI gates the coding agent cannot modify</li> <li>A record of engaging with the research community, such as publications, tool papers, or upstream open source contributions in program analysis or security</li> </ul> <h3><strong>About the team</strong></h3> <p>The Security Factory: Code Scanning team develops GitLab's SAST capabilities for customer software repositories.</p> <p>We work closely with the Code Security team on scanning rules & flows, with Composition Analysis on the broader software supply chain, and with other groups across the Sec Section. We rely heavily on asynchronous work across time zones.</p> <div class="c-message_actions__container c-message__actions"> </div> <div><span style="font-size: xx-small;"><span style="color: white;">Remote-Global</span></span></div><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. challenges.</li> <li value="7">Familiarity with Git, software development tools, or application lifecycle management, and ability to learn GitLab’s platform.</li> <li value="8">Alignment with GitLab’s description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps.
